subject: CAIQ matrix concordance, sampling plan, and evidence custody checklist
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@polarisbank.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: polaris-security@polarisbank.com
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ crosswalk and evidence — upcoming audit window (Aug 2-4)

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the quick chat yesterday. Polaris is scheduled for a pre-audit review the week of Aug 2 and our external auditor has requested a CAIQ crosswalk that maps your CSA controls to our internal control IDs, plus a lightweight sampling plan for runtime evidence (logs, key rotation records, access review snapshots). Can you confirm:

- A representative who will own the CAIQ mapping deliverable
- What evidence you can provide for controls CCM_02, CCM_08, CCM_11, CCM_13 and CCM_17, and any known gaps
- A list of artifacts you can drop in our secure SFTP or a Drive folder by July 22

For scope: this is hosted inference only (no Private deployment in scope). If feasible, we’d also like a short custody checklist that documents where artifacts live, retention, and escalation for redaction requests.

Appreciate it — auditor is picky about filenames and traceability.

Best,
Elena Morris
Senior InfoSec Manager, Polaris Bank
[polaris-security@polarisbank.com]

[Attachment: audit-schedule.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@polarisbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ crosswalk and evidence — upcoming audit window (Aug 2-4)

Elena —

Thanks for the clear scope. I’ll own the CAIQ crosswalk and deliver the mapping + initial evidence index. Quick plan:

1) We’ll produce a CAIQ concordance spreadsheet that maps Redwood control statements to Polaris control IDs, indicate whether the control is implemented (Yes/Partial/No), and point to evidence filenames.
2) Sampling plan: for runtime controls we’ll include log window definitions, sampling heuristic (1 day of peak traffic + 1 day random within last 90d), and validation notes.
3) Artifacts: we can stage required items to the Drive link you shared (or SFTP if you prefer) by Jul 21 EOD.
4) Custody checklist: short PDF listing storage, retention, redaction workflow, and owners.

I’m copying Kimberly (security litigator / evidence coordinator) and Jordan (controls and runtime telemetry lead) to help assemble artifacts and confirm access.

Deliverables and tentative owners:
- caiq_concordance_v1.xlsx — Markus (owner)
- evidence_custody_checklist.pdf — Kimberly (owner)
- runtime_sample_index.txt — Jordan (owner)

Can you confirm the Drive vs SFTP preference and whether auditors need DocuSign-ready attestation statements?

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Compliance & Controls
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: none]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 08:19:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ crosswalk and evidence — upcoming audit window (Aug 2-4)

Markus / Jordan —

Thanks — I’ll draft the custody checklist and handle the redaction/escalation section. A few practical asks before we package:

- Can Jordan enumerate exact artifact names and retention timestamps for runtime logs (we need the extraction path and sample IDs so Polaris can verify traceability).
- We should flag controls with third-party dependencies (e.g., CC-3rdParty-Auth) so the auditor understands where attestations vs artifacts live.
- For any partials, include remediation ETA and mitigating compensating controls in the concordance. Don’t call everything \"partial\" without a short rationale.

Marissa — looping you for Docs/Links help — please create a Drive folder at the HubSpot link and set viewer access for polaris-security@polarisbank.com. Use the naming convention: PLR-2027-034_CAIX_DELIVERABLES (note: please confirm final folder name with Markus).

I’ll start the checklist draft and attach a template.

Kimberly Park
Principal, Security & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: custody_checklist_template.pdf (application/pdf)]

Subject: Re: CAIQ crosswalk and evidence — upcoming audit window (Aug 2-4)

Elena / team —

Quick technical breakdown attached and included inline for convenience.

Summary points:
- Runtime logs: we will export two 24-hour windows (peak-day: 2027-06-18, random-day: 2027-05-11) covering the inference control trace (request_id, model_variant, region, auth_token_id, TTL, KV-cache-hits). Filenames: inference_trace_20270618.ndjson, inference_trace_20270511.ndjson.
- Key rotation records: KMS rotation events for customer KMS integrations and Redwood-managed keys between 2027-01-01 and 2027-07-01. Filename: kms_rotation_events_20270101-20270701.csv.
- Access reviews: snapshot of IAM group membership as of 2027-06-30 (iam_review_20270630.csv).
- Known control partials: CCM_11 (data classification enforcement for ephemeral caches) — partial; remediation ETA 2027-09-01; compensating control: short-lived KV cache TTL + encrypted at rest.

I attached the first-pass concordance (caiq_concordance_v1.xlsx) and a runtime_sample_index.txt that lists offsets/linecounts for quick auditor pulls.

Elena — posting these to the Drive link now per request; please confirm SFTP preference if you’d rather.

Jordan Blake
Lead, Runtime Telemetry & Observability
Redwood Inference
